reference: GNU coreutils touch is the parity oracle. The independent system /usr/bin/stat observes nanosecond timestamps, size and mode on both arms; fixture paths are relative. Tree comparison also verifies bytes, modes and links. Bash type/help are metadata contracts only.
coverage: Default creation under umask 022 and preservation of existing file bytes.
-c no-create behavior, -- option termination, and relative names containing spaces or a leading dash.
-d/--date epoch timestamps with positive nanoseconds and a negative fractional epoch.
-a and -m timestamp selection while preserving the other timestamp.
-r reference timestamp copying and POSIX -t timestamp parsing.
-h symlink timestamp updates without changing the target.
Invalid date diagnostics/status and continued processing of later operands.
GNU argument-error statuses for missing values, invalid values and unknown options.
Default symlink following, directory timestamps and hardlink timestamp identity.
exclusions: This suite does not exhaustively cover GNU natural-language date parsing, every long-option spelling, fractional precision beyond nanoseconds, inaccessible filesystems, or all error diagnostics.
The fixture compares timestamps through GNU stat output; the generic tree snapshot does not include timestamps.

cases.purpose: Default touch creates an empty file with mode 0644 under the runner's umask 022 and leaves existing binary contents intact.
cases.script: printf 'payload\000x' > keep; touch fresh keep; [[ -f fresh && $(/usr/bin/stat -c '%a:%s' fresh) == 644:0 && $(/usr/bin/stat -c %s keep) == 9 ]] || exit 1; printf 'created empty 0644 file; kept 9 bytes\n'

cases.purpose: -c leaves a missing relative operand absent; -- allows creation of a leading-dash name, and a spaced operand is handled as one path.
cases.script: touch -c -- absent; [[ ! -e absent ]] || exit 1; touch -- '-leading' 'two words'; [[ -f '-leading' && -f 'two words' ]] || exit 1; printf 'no-create and option terminator honored\n'

cases.purpose: -d and --date preserve subsecond precision and normalize a negative fractional epoch; GNU stat renders both timestamp fields independently.
cases.script: touch -d @1234567890.123456789 positive; touch --date=@-0.25 negative; /usr/bin/stat -c '%n %x | %y' positive negative

cases.purpose: -a updates only access time and -m updates only modification time, with the untouched timestamp retained across each operation.
cases.script: touch -d @1000000000 item; touch -a -d @2000000000 item; access_only=$(/usr/bin/stat -c '%X:%Y' item); [[ $access_only == 2000000000:1000000000 ]] || exit 1; touch -m -d @3000000000 item; modify_only=$(/usr/bin/stat -c '%X:%Y' item); [[ $modify_only == 2000000000:3000000000 ]] || exit 1; printf '%s\n%s\n' "$access_only" "$modify_only"

cases.purpose: -r copies both timestamps, including nanoseconds, from a relative reference file onto an existing target.
cases.script: touch -d @1234567890.987654321 reference; touch target; touch -r reference target; /usr/bin/stat -c '%n %x | %y' reference target

cases.purpose: POSIX -t with the seconds field sets both file timestamps to the specified UTC calendar time.
-h timestamps the symlink itself while leaving its relative target's timestamps unchanged.
cases.script: touch -d @1000000000 target; ln -s target link; touch -h -d @2000000000 link; link_time=$(/usr/bin/stat -c '%X:%Y' link); target_time=$(/usr/bin/stat -L -c '%X:%Y' link); [[ $link_time == 2000000000:2000000000 && $target_time == 1000000000:1000000000 ]] || exit 1; printf 'link=%s target=%s\n' "$link_time" "$target_time"

cases.purpose: An invalid --date value is rejected before creating the requested file; GNU touch returns status 1 and emits a diagnostic.
A failed first operand does not prevent touch from processing a later valid relative operand; the overall invocation reports failure.
cases.script: if touch absent/child survivor; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; [[ $rc == 1 && -f survivor ]] || exit 1; printf 'failed operand reported; later operand created\n'

cases.purpose: Bash exposes touch as a builtin and its help advertises the timestamp-changing contract and --date spelling.
cases.script: [[ $(type -t touch) == builtin ]] || exit 1; touch_help=$(help touch) || exit 1; [[ $touch_help == *'change file timestamps'* && $touch_help == *'--date=DATE'* ]] || exit 1; printf 'touch builtin and documented help available\n'
cases.stdout: touch builtin and documented help available

cases.script: touch -d @100 target; ln -s target link; touch -d @200 link; /usr/bin/stat -c '%X:%Y' target

cases.purpose: Timestamp a directory and a hardlinked regular file without changing link identity or contents.
cases.script: mkdir box; printf data > original; ln original alias; touch -d @123 box alias; /usr/bin/stat -c '%X:%Y' box original alias
